# Generating sound effects

A `generate-sfx` command is installed. It turns a text description into a
short sound-effect audio file and saves it into your project as a regular
static asset — the RIGHT way to give a game or toy real audio. Do not
synthesize bleeps with the Web Audio oscillator API when a real sound would
fit, and do not hotlink audio from random external sites.

```
generate-sfx "retro arcade laser zap, short and punchy" --out sfx/laser.wav
generate-sfx "heavy wooden door slowly creaking open" --duration 3 --out sfx/door.wav
generate-sfx "gentle rain on a tin roof, distant thunder" --duration 10 --loop --out sfx/rain.wav
```

- `--out` (default: a slug of the description in the current directory):
  write the wav here; put sounds in a `sfx/` folder inside /workspace so
  they publish with the project.
- `--duration` (0.5-30 seconds): omit to let the model pick a natural
  length. Game SFX are usually best at 0.5-2 seconds.
- `--loop`: makes the clip loop seamlessly — use for ambience and
  atmosphere beds, then set `audio.loop = true` when playing it.

Describe the SOUND, not a scene: adjectives + material + action ("metallic
coin clink, bright, short") beat narrative descriptions. The command prints
the saved path and clip length when it succeeds.

Using the files is plain web audio — they work in the preview AND on the
published site (they're just files, no platform runtime needed):

```
const zap = new Audio("./sfx/laser.wav");
// per shot: clone so rapid-fire sounds can overlap
zap.cloneNode().play();
```

Browsers block audio until the user's first interaction — start playback
from input handlers (click/keydown), never on page load.

Budget the generation: a small set of distinct sounds (3-6) covers most
games, the API allows 10 per minute and 100 per day, and each call takes a
few seconds. The daily quota is shared across every project and session on
the account — if you are told it is exhausted, retrying will not help until
it resets, so work with the sounds already in the workspace.
Generate a sound ONCE and reuse the file across edits — never regenerate
sounds that already exist in the workspace on later turns, and never call
generate-sfx in a loop.
